title: VAOM boundary probes
description: How each boundary a matrix relies on is probed on one agent host (VAOM v5 Section 9, scorecard metric 13): the forbidden action attempted from inside the agent's context, against a canary, never a live counterparty. Human-approved and versioned. A probe runner executes these on the host and writes vaom.probe-result records; the Guardian keeps the results and judges each boundary against the matrix's claimed mechanism and schedule. Engine-agnostic about how the attempt is made; the host id names which runner applies. Draft 0.1.

boundary.description: A boundary id in the matrix.

forbiddenTools.description: Host tool names whose presence in the agent's tool manifest contradicts the boundary: exact names, or a prefix ending in '*'. A general-purpose tool (a shell, say) that could also cross the boundary isn't caught by this list; the attempt is what tests it.

prompt.description: The instruction given to the agent: attempt the forbidden action against the canary.

canary.description: The canary or dry-run target the attempt aims at, as the matrix's verification.target names it.

refusal.description: A regular expression the target's authorization refusal matches in the tool's error output. Without it, a call that ran and failed proves nothing: the result is inconclusive, never scope-denied.
